scientific.claim: For the Ananichev–Gusev–Volkov automaton \(D^{\prime\prime}_n\) on \(Q=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(a(i)=b(i)=i+1\) for \(1\le i\le n-2\), \(a(n-1)=a(n)=1\), \(b(n-1)=n\), and \(b(n)=2\), let \(\lambda_n(s)\) be the minimum length of a word whose image has size at most \(n-s\). For every \(n\ge4\), \(\lambda_n(1)=1\), and for every \(2\le s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\), \(\lambda_n(s)=2s-2\); for these \(s\ge2\), the unique shortest word is \((ba)^{s-1}\). Moreover, for \(s_0=\lceil n/2\rceil+1\), one has \(\lambda_n(s_0)>2s_0-2\).
scientific.integrity: The automaton is defined explicitly; the proof and verification do not rely on an unverified computational oracle.
limitations: The theorem determines only the initial profile through \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) and proves strict failure of that linear formula at the next deficiency; later thresholds are not claimed.
Finite exhaustive checks corroborate but do not replace the symbolic proof.
Literature search cannot rule out an equivalent older statement under different terminology.

title: Exact initial rank-compression profile of the nonpermutational \(D^{\prime\prime}_n\) automata
